Thebes, the most powerful polis in Boeotia, rose in revolt and besieged the Macedonian garrison on the Cadmea. The exiled Athenian statesman Demosthenes also supported the uprising, sending arms. Alexander force-marched his army south in 13 days, catching the Thebans off guard. He stormed the city, razed it to the ground, killed about 6,000 Thebans, and sold the remaining 30,000 survivors into slavery. The destruction of Thebes became a lasting symbol of Macedonian ruthlessness, deterring other Greek states from revolting. No opposing tag exists for Thebes/Boeotia. Chen Sheng Wu Guang Uprising | The first great popular revolt against Qin rule: conscripted soldiers Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, delayed by rains en route to their posting, incite their fellow conscripts to rebel under the slogan 'the strong will first perish' (209 BC). The rebellion sweeps through the Yangtze-Huai region, briefly establishing a Chu restoration state under Chen Sheng's self-proclaimed 'King of Chu.' Though crushed by Qin forces within months, it sparks the cascade of uprisings that ultimately destroy the Qin dynasty. No opposing tag exists for the rebel faction -- the Chu restoration state had no independent tag of its own until cp_western_chu was later established. Mutiny at Opis | At Opis on the Tigris in 324 BC, Alexander announced his plans to send home the Macedonian veterans and integrate Persians into the army. The Macedonian troops, already resentful of Alexander's adoption of Persian court customs and his appointment of Persians to high commands, mutinied openly. Alexander executed 13 ringleaders, then withdrew to his quarters for two days, refusing to meet the soldiers. When the army's resolve wavered, Alexander finally emerged and delivered a speech dismissing the entire army, telling them to tell their fathers that they had abandoned their king among foreigners. The soldiers broke down, begged forgiveness, and were reconciled. A great feast of 9,000 guests symbolised unity of Macedonians and Persians. The general Coenus (who had also led the earlier Hyphasis mutiny) served as the soldiers' spokesman. 'particularist_rebels' used as the closest existing type for a mutiny of Macedonian veterans defending their privileged identity against universalist integration.
